sections.skill: Write a clear quote with inclusions, exclusions and validity

questions.prompt: What does a quote tell a customer?

choices.text: How much the business paid for its last tax return
Which competitor charges the lowest price nearby
How many hours the owner slept last week
What a job will cost before work begins

questions.correct_answer: What a job will cost before work begins
questions.intro: A QUOTE (or estimate) tells a customer what a job will cost before work begins. A PROPOSAL adds more detail: the problem, what you will deliver, the timeline, the price and the terms. A clear quote lists what IS included and what is NOT, how long the price is valid (for example 30 days), and any deposit required. Build the price from your costs and time, not from a guess. Vague quotes ("about 500, maybe more") lead to arguments later.
questions.feedback: A quote prices the job in advance.

sections.skill: A restaurant menu with a clear price

questions.prompt: Which menu line is clearer?

choices.text: "Burger with fries, 12 dollars; cheese 1 dollar extra"
"Food, about 10 dollars, maybe more, depending on the day"

questions.correct_answer: "Burger with fries, 12 dollars; cheese 1 dollar extra"
questions.intro: A good menu says "Burger with fries, 12 dollars; cheese is 1 dollar extra." You know what you get and what costs more. A bad menu says "Food, about 10, maybe more." A quote should read like the good menu: what is included, what is extra, and the price, so nobody is surprised when the bill arrives.
